newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. localities may get $70 mln more for welfare.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. localities may get $70 mln more for welfare.

text.p: New York State's localities might get another $70 million for welfare from the federal government if Washington makes a technical change, a spokesman for the state budget office said.

"We believe it's just a technical adjustment and Congress will make the adjustment to allow us to use the money in a flexible way," said John Signor, a spokesman for the state budget division, earlier this week.

The funds would not raise how much the state stands to collect from its approximately $2.4 billion federal block grant, the spokesman added. "It comes from the block grant, but under the block grant there's some flexibility in how you spend some of the money."
He explained that localities could use the money to replace dollars they would have had to come up to pay for a range of services for welfare recipients, including childcare, and job training.
